newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/14.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/14.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 14.0/14.5 percent on Wednesday after edging to an early high of 17.0 percent, dealers said.
One state bank dealer said liquidity seemed to improve as more funds returned to the system.
Dealers said the small early fluctuation might have resulted from an extended neutral central bank money policy.
"I think the market may ease further in the afternoon if trades are cleared in time," one local bank dealer said, adding that longer-term rates were a bit high.
One-week money was last at 13.75/14.00 and one-month at 13.50/13.75 percent.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates stable, offering one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 16.51 percent, compared with 17.69 percent on Monday.

Bond dealers said prices remained stable, with focus seen on primary issues. One dealer said the 500 billion rupiah seven-year straight bonds of Bank DKI, with a fixed coupon of 15.5 for the first year, was the most sought one.
She said investors remained cautious on bonds to be issued by property companies.
